plain_english_title: Cardiovascular System Guide: Heart METs vs. Ejection Fraction, Hypertension vs. Heart Hypertrophy & Vascular Rules
what_this_means: Cardiovascular claims combine complex medical metrics—METs exercise capacity, Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction (LVEF), blood pressure readings, and ankle/toe vascular pressures—with high-stakes effective-date rules for Agent Orange Ischemic Heart Disease (Nehmer, 38 C.F.R. § 3.816) and PACT Act Hypertension (38 U.S.C. § 1116). This comparison explains the three eras of heart ratings (pre-January 12, 1998; the 1998–2021 LVEF + METs era; and the post-November 14, 2021 METs-centered General Heart Formula), when 0% or 10% Hypertension (Diagnostic Code 7101) must step up to 30%+ Hypertensive Heart Disease (Diagnostic Code 7007), and how implanted defibrillators, arrhythmias, peripheral arterial disease, and cold injuries are rated.
record_clues: A pre-November 14, 2021 Ischemic Heart Disease (Diagnostic Code 7005) or Hypertensive Heart Disease (Diagnostic Code 7007) rating assigning 10% based on >7–10 METs while ignoring an echocardiogram showing LVEF of 30%–50% (60%) or <30% (100%), or LVH/hypertrophy (30%).

A running pre-November 14, 2021 60% or 100% LVEF-based heart rating unlawfully reduced after November 14, 2021 without actual medical improvement (void under 38 U.S.C. § 1155 and 38 C.F.R. § 3.951(a)).

Service-connected Hypertension (Diagnostic Code 7101) rated at 0% or 10% when an echocardiogram or cardiac MRI shows left ventricular hypertrophy or dilatation—warranting evaluation as Hypertensive Heart Disease (Diagnostic Code 7007 at 30% or higher)—or secondary kidney/eye complications.

Sustained ventricular arrhythmia (Diagnostic Code 7011) rated below 100% while an Automatic Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillator (AICD) is in place, or diabetic Peripheral Arterial Disease (Diagnostic Code 7114) rated on calcified ABI without toe pressure / TcPO2 testing.
important_cautions: Ischemic Heart Disease vs. Hypertension under Nehmer: Ischemic Heart Disease (Diagnostic Code 7005) IS a covered Nehmer condition eligible for pre-2010 retroactive effective dates under 38 C.F.R. § 3.816, whereas PACT Act § 404 Hypertension (Diagnostic Code 7101) is excluded from Nehmer class retroactivity (though previously denied survivor DIC claims can be re-evaluated retroactively under 38 U.S.C. § 1305).

Blood-pressure medication rule in Diagnostic Code 7101: the Veterans Court held en banc in McCarroll v. McDonald that Diagnostic Code 7101 contemplates controlled blood pressure on continuous medication at 10%, so higher 20%/40%/60% hypertension tiers require actual diastolic/systolic readings rather than speculative unmedicated estimates (also note Note (1)'s '3 different days' confirmation rule applies to initial diagnosis, not increased-rating exams).

Do not cite standalone LVEF for claims filed on or after November 14, 2021, or cite 1998 LVEF/METs rules for Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) before January 12, 1998, and remember 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c) permits only one final merits CUE decision per prior Board issue.
VA's February 17, 2026 § 4.10 medication rule (91 FR 7118) was formally rescinded on February 27, 2026 (91 FR 9712) and is not active law.
questions_for_representative: If I have service-connected Hypertension (Diagnostic Code 7101), does an echocardiogram or cardiac MRI show left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) supporting a 30% or higher rating under Diagnostic Code 7007—or secondary kidney or retinal damage?
Did VA check both my METs workload and—for any claim period between January 12, 1998 and November 13, 2021—my Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction (LVEF)?

If I have an implanted AICD defibrillator (Diagnostic Code 7011) or cold injury residuals in multiple extremities (Diagnostic Code 7122), are all separate ratings and Special Monthly Compensation rules applied?
If I am a Vietnam or Blue Water Navy Veteran (or survivor) with Ischemic Heart Disease, have we audited earlier claims and medical diagnoses for a Nehmer effective date under 38 C.F.R. § 3.816?
